(ii) 12th respondent in persisting to enforce the punishment despite hue and cry from the petitioner due to unbearable pain by giving deaf hearing to it;

Contents of the affidavit, filed by the mother of the minor daughter, who is Writ Petitioner, in support of the Writ Petition, in brief, are that, the petitioner is studying V standard in Variant Primary School, Eluru and pursuing studies in the said school from Nursery onwards; that 12th respondent is the Principal of the said school and she teaches four (04) subjects to V class students,
and husband of 12th respondent is the Correspondent of the said school, as such, there is no authority over her in the school.

sentences.text: (b) The petitioner was suffering from Typhoid, food poison etc., resulting in significant drop of platelets count, severe digestion issues and the petitioner was medically advised not to wear tight SRK, J clothing; that due to deteriorating health condition of petitioner and non-cooperation of 12th respondent, the petitioner was not sent to school for about one month; that though the petitioner was interested to attend school in spite of her poor health condition, 12th respondent did not allow her to attend classes in civil dress; that the petitioner and her parents were in fear of the attitude of 12th respondent in insisting the petitioner to sit on the floor of the class as punishment.

(c) That upon the request made by the mother of petitioner, with great difficulty, 12th respondent gave permission to the petitioner, by allowing her to attend the school, in civil dress on health grounds for one day, and on the next day, 12th respondent refused to allow the petitioner and made her to sit separately on the floor as punishment; that on 05.03.2025, again the petitioner was forced to sit on the floor of the class, though the petitioner's mother requested not to do so and when the petitioner started crying, 12th respondent threatened her with dire consequences and caused humiliation to the petitioner.

(d) That when the mother of petitioner along with her family friend viz. Nitta Swarna Latha, rushed to the school, 12th respondent remained adamant and refused to allow the petitioner SRK, J to sit on the bench, justifying it as disciplinary action; that 12th respondent placed her hand on the mother of petitioner and her family friend and dismissively told them to leave the school.
Besides the above, it is the allegation of mother of petitioner that there is no Fitness Certificate and No Objection Certificate obtained from concerned departments.
That the mother of petitioner gave complaint to the respondents and on 07.03.2025, both were called to the office of 5th respondent for Inquiry.

Instead of cooperating with the process of Inquiry, 12th respondent deliberately escalated the situation by bringing around thirty (30) members to 5th respondent office and they shouted at the parents of petitioner, abused them and created an atmosphere of fear and intimidation.

(e) That the respondent No.12, to divert the attention from her, instructed the staff members to spread a forwarded message and falsely portrayed 12th respondent as a victim in the hands of Mullu Mananya vs The State Of Ap on 11 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127175205/
5 mother of petitioner, which act is a serious violation of ethical standards; that there is no spontaneous action either from the end of 5th respondent or from 3rd respondent, unless some preventive steps are taken by respondents, the unsafe environment would prevail and be continued against the petitioner.

sentences.text: Hence, the Writ Petition.

SRK, J 3. Respondent No.5 filed counter-affidavit, stating that on 06.03.2025, a complaint was received from the mother of petitioner, narrating the aforesaid issue and the Deputy Educational Officer,
Eluru was directed to conduct an Inquiry.

In the Report submitted by the Deputy Educational Officer, Eluru, it was stated that 12th respondent accepted that the petitioner was instructed to sit on the floor; that 12th respondent stated that only for discipline purpose, they instructed the students, who come late to school without uniform, to sit on the floor; that 12th respondent does not know about the severity of health condition of petitioner and that, she had no discrimination on any of the child; that 12th respondent tendered excuse for the mistake occurred, as she was unaware of illness of the petitioner at that time; that 12th respondent stated that the mother of petitioner and her family friend warned her over phone by some unknown persons and she would be imprisoned for two years.

(b) A Show-Cause notice was issued vide Rc.No.1002/A1/ 2025, dated 07.03.2025 to the School Management regarding the issue; that 12th respondent in her reply stated that she was unaware of the health condition of the petitioner and the parents of the petitioner did not submit Medical Certificate to the school about SRK, J her illness; that 12th respondent was informed to allow the child to the school to attend examinations as per the direction of this Court and 12th respondent also gave assurance in that regard, but the petitioner and two other persons came to the District Educational Office and stated that they could not send the petitioner to school without any written statement from the school authority. Respondent No.6 conducted detailed Inquiry among 20 parents, who stated that it is not a big issue towards simple punishment.
The parents of petitioners also accepted that there was no issue with the school for the past seven years.
Hence, it is prayed to dismiss the Writ Petition.

4. Respondent No.12 filed counter-affidavit, denying the contents of the affidavit filed in support of the Writ Petitioner, inter alia, contending that on 05.03.2025, the petitioner came to school late and as a disciplinary measure, she was instructed to sit on the floor for a limited period and later, she was allowed to sit on the bench along with other students, and this practice is being implemented in their school for several years and no parent raised objection or found fault with the Management therefor.

That she noticed that the petitioner was feeling unwell and immediately, 12th respondent spoke to petitioner's mother and at that time, she did SRK, J not inform to 12th respondent that the petitioner was suffering from serious illness; that the mother of petitioner along with her friend Nitta Swarnalatha came to school, started shouting and started recording the entire incident through her mobile; that one of the Advocates called 12th respondent to her mobile and spoke to her in abusive language and insisted her to give unconditional apology and threatened her that she would be put in jail for two years if she did not do so.

6 (b) That the parent of the petitioner and the persons who accompanied her on the date of the incident, were not in a position to listen to the words of 12th respondent and if really the petitioner is not well, she ought not to have been sent to school.

sentences.text: If any student is found ill, the Management would inform the same to their parents and 12th respondent did the same.
But the petitioner's mother in response to such intimation, approached the institution in a very high-handed manner.

Respondent No.12 agreed before 10th respondent to tender apology stating that she was unaware about the health of the petitioner and to undertake that she would be more careful in future, but one Nitta Swarnalatha, who accompanied mother of petitioner, was not convinced with that, forced 12th respondent to sign on the apology letter drafted by her;
SRK, J that 5th respondent called the parent and Management for Inquiry, on 07.03.2025 before the Deputy Educational Officer, Eluru Division and even before the said authority, Nitta Swarnalatha, who accompanied petitioner's mother, shouted against 12th respondent using abusive language.

The unwanted interference of persons, who accompanied petitioner's mother created the entire mess, which not only damaged the reputation of the institution but also spoiled the mind of the petitioner; that the action of petitioner's mother and her friend caused severe mental agony to 12th respondent.
Hence, it is prayed to dismiss the Writ Petition with exemplary costs.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the entire incident occurred only due to the attitude of 12th respondent, as she insisted the petitioner to sit on the floor of the class towards punishment, though she is well aware of the fact that the petitioner was suffering from ill health.

Learned Government Pleader for School Education representing respondent No.5 would contend that in the Inquiry conducted by 5th respondent, 12th respondent accepted that she instructed the petitioner to sit on the floor, as she came to school late and without proper uniform and such punishment is only for discipline purpose.

Learned Government Pleader would further contend that 12th respondent tendered apology during Inquiry as she was unaware of illness of the petitioner,
and stated she will be more careful in future.

7. Learned counsel for 12th respondent would contend that as the petitioner came late to the school and as a part of disciplinary measure, 12th respondent instructed the petitioner to sit on the floor for a limited period but the mother of petitioner along with her friend Nitta Swarnalatha raised objection and found fault with the said act and high-handedly rushed to the school premises and shouted over 12th respondent.
Learned counsel would further contend that 12th respondent was threatened that she will be put in jail for two years if she did not tender apology.

According to the SRK, J learned counsel, the entire incident occurred only due to high- handed approach of mother of petitioner and her family friend towards 12th respondent and their acts damaged the reputation of the school.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the Writ Petitioner, learned Government Pleader for School Education representing respondent No.5 and learned counsel for the respondent No.12 and perused the entire material available on record.

9. A perusal of entire material on record goes to show the crux of the case that, the petitioner, who is studying V standard in Variant Primary School, Eluru, was insisted by 12th respondent, who is Principal of the aforesaid school, to sit on the floor of the class on 05.03.2025.
As per the version of mother of petitioner, the petitioner was suffering from severe ill-health by that time.
A perusal of the affidavit filed by the mother of petitioner goes to show that prior to the incident, the petitioner was absent for one month.

Having regard to the final examinations, to revise the syllabus, the mother of petitioner sent her to school on 05.03.2025 in civil dress, and late, and as a disciplinary measure,
12th respondent insisted the petitioner to sit on the floor for a limited period.
SRK, J 10.

As regards the issue of informing the School Management about the health issue by the parents of petitioner, 12th respondent, who also teaches four (04) subjects to V standard students, during Inquiry before 5th respondent, fairly stated that she insisted the petitioner to sit on the floor of the class, as she came to school late and without proper uniform and she was totally unaware about the ill health and it is 12th respondent, who informed to the parents of petitioner, and later they learnt about the incident.

Indisputably, the mother of petitioner might have informed about the health condition of petitioner to the School Management, but it is nowhere stated in the affidavit, that 12th respondent was aware of the health condition of the petitioner.
Then, it cannot be expected that 12th respondent was fully aware of the health condition of petitioner and she intentionally insisted the petitioner to sit on the floor of the class.

11. A perusal of the material on record goes to show that basing on the Complaint, dated 06.03.2025 made by mother of petitioner to 5th respondent, Show-cause Notice vide R.C.No.1002/ A1/2025,
dated 07.03.2025, was issued to the Variant Primary School Management, Eluru and 12th respondent to submit their explanation in regard to the allegations made by mother of SRK, J petitioner.

In reply to the Show-cause Notice, dated 07.03.2025, 12th respondent submitted her explanation on 07.03.2025 stating that on 05.03.2025 the petitioner was sent in civil dress and late,
to school and as a disciplinary measure, 12th respondent asked the petitioner and other children,
who came late to school, to sit on the floor of the class.

It is the version of 12th respondent that she noticed that the petitioner was unwell and as such, she made a phone call to her mother and at that time, mother of petitioner neither submitted Medical Certificate of petitioner nor informed to 12th respondent over phone about the health condition, but high- handedly entered into the school premises and abused 12th respondent and the school management and damaged the school reputation.

12. The Deputy Educational Officer, Eluru Division, Eluru vide R.C.No.38/Dy.E.O./Eluru, dated 07.03.2025 conducted Inquiry over the entire incident by examining the mother of petitioner and 12th respondent in the presence of the Assistant Director-II.

A perusal of the Inquiry Report goes to show that on the date of the incident, when the petitioner left to school, 12th respondent was in Mullu Mananya vs The State Of Ap on 11 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127175205/
8 classroom upstairs.

sentences.text:
Their inquiry further revealed that the students, who attend late to the school,
the school, as a disciplinary SRK, J measure, School Management insists the students to sit on the floor of the class for a limited period and later, they will be asked to sit on the bench along with other students and there is no discrimination in implementing such disciplinary measure among the students.

Indeed, 12th respondent, during inquiry by the Deputy Educational Officer, Eluru, stated that the mistake occurred as she was unaware of the petitioner's health condition and she fairly tendered apology in respect of the incident occurred and she gave assurance that she will be more careful in future.

But, as per Inquiry Report, it goes to show that father of petitioner did not show interest in the petitioner's education and her mother anticipates that 12th respondent was causing trouble to petitioner and they insisted for a written apology and refused to accept the compromise with 12th respondent.

13. Though, learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the Inquiry Report is not in accordance with law, they did not challenge the same appropriate Forum, but straightaway filed the present Writ Petition.

In fact, the Final Examinations in respect of V standard were already completed, therefore, question of interference by 12th respondent in petitioner's education and examination process does not arise.
SRK, J 14.

A perusal of the contents of the Inquiry Report goes to show that 12th respondent, though was unaware of petitioner's health condition, is fair enough in tendering apology to the parents of petitioner during Inquiry conducted by the Deputy Educational Officer, Eluru and moreover, she gave assurance that she will be more careful in future.

When such is the fair act done by 12th respondent having regard to the education of petitioner, the petitioner, who studied in the said school from Nursery to present V standard, her parents might not have insisted her to submit written apology.

Indeed, on 20.03.2025 the Deputy Educational Officer, Eluru and the Head Master of MPPS Sriram Nagar(S), Eluru randomly conducted inquiry over Parents, Teachers and Principal regarding imposition of punishments to the students of the school, for which, most of them expressed that the punishment of insisting the students, who came to school late or without proper uniform, to sit on the floor of the class for a limited period, is not a major punishment and it is a part of disciplinary activity.

Even, the parents of petitioner also participated in the said questionnaire and they too stated that they are aware of the said punishment and they only differ the present issue, for the reason that the petitioner was suffering from ill health by that time.
Except the above, the parents SRK, J of petitioner also did not complain against the activities of the school.

15. Therefore, having regard to the entire facts and circumstances of the case, this Court did not find any ground to grant the relief as sought by the petitioner and the Writ Petition is devoid of merit and force and it is deserved to be dismissed.
16.
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending if any, shall also stand closed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In reply to the Show-cause Notice, dated 07.03.2025, 12th respondent submitted her explanation on 07.03.2025 stating that on 05.03.2025 the petitioner was sent in civil dress and late,
to school and as a disciplinary measure, 12th respondent asked the petitioner and other children,
who came late to school, to sit on the floor of the class.
It is the version of 12th respondent that she noticed that the petitioner was unwell and as such, she made a phone call to her mother and at that time, mother of petitioner neither submitted Medical Certificate of petitioner nor informed to 12th respondent over phone about the health condition, but high- handedly entered into the school premises and abused 12th respondent and the school management and damaged the school reputation.
But, as per Inquiry Report, it goes to show that father of petitioner did not show interest in the petitioner's education and her mother anticipates that 12th respondent was causing trouble to petitioner and they insisted for a written apology and refused to accept the compromise with 12th respondent.
In fact, the Final Examinations in respect of V standard were already completed, therefore, question of interference by 12th respondent in petitioner's education and examination process does not arise.
A perusal of the contents of the Inquiry Report goes to show that 12th respondent, though was unaware of petitioner's health condition, is fair enough in tendering apology to the parents of petitioner during Inquiry conducted by the Deputy Educational Officer, Eluru and moreover, she gave assurance that she will be more careful in future.
15. Therefore, having regard to the entire facts and circumstances of the case, this Court did not find any ground to grant the relief as sought by the petitioner and the Writ Petition is devoid of merit and force and it is deserved to be dismissed.
